source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: Why does the lecture call computer use 'genuinely difficult,' rather than a solved problem?

options.text: Because screenshots take up too much storage space to be practical
options.feedback: Storage is not the issue raised. The difficulty described is about completing tasks correctly, not about how much space images occupy.

options.text: Because most software is not built to be operated with a mouse and keyboard
options.feedback: Everyday software is built exactly for mouse-and-keyboard use by people, which is why an agent has to learn to click and type the way a person does. That is not the source of the difficulty.

options.text: Because the model must translate between two programming languages at each step
options.feedback: No language translation is involved. The work is interpreting an image and choosing where to click or type, which is a different kind of problem entirely.

options.text: Because even the best systems today finish only some of the tasks people find easy
options.feedback: Realistic desktop benchmarks are the evidence the lecture leans on: current systems fall well short of what a person does without thinking about it, which is what keeps this an open problem rather than a finished one.
